artworks.title: Amphiaraus
artworks.description: Fontainebleau-school engraving by Domenico del Barbiere in the Metropolitan Museum of Art: the Argive seer Amphiaraus, who foresaw his death in the war of the Seven against Thebes yet marched when Eriphyle, bribed with Harmonia's necklace, forced his hand. Renaissance print culture made the reluctant prophet a type of doomed foresight.

artworks.title: Votive Relief of Amphiaraus from Oropos
artworks.description: Marble votive from the Amphiareion at Oropos, now in the National Archaeological Museum, Athens: Amphiaraus appears in the healing type of Asclepius, accompanied by a younger attendant. The relief shows the seer's afterlife as oracle-hero — swallowed by the earth before Thebes, worshipped where the sick slept for dreams.

artworks.title: Amphiaraus Betrayed by His Wife (maiolica bowl)
artworks.description: Urbino istoriato maiolica by Francesco Xanto Avelli: Amphiaraus betrayed by Eriphyle, the wife who sold him into the Theban war for a necklace. The bowl turns the Argive household drama into colorful Renaissance narrative ware — the seer's forced departure painted for the table.

artworks.title: Votive Relief of Archinos to Amphiaraos
artworks.description: Marble shrine-relief of the offering of Archinos to Amphiaraos: the hero-healer stands treating a youth's shoulder, while the same youth sleeps on a couch as a sacred snake glides over him — incubation made visible. The inscription names Amphiaraos; the piece is the classic image of the Oropos oracle-cult that followed the seer's disappearance into the earth.

popCulture.title: Seven Against Thebes
popCulture.creator: Aeschylus
popCulture.description: Aeschylus' reluctant prophet at the seventh gate — Amphiaraus marches knowing he will die, bribed into war by Eriphyle.

popCulture.title: Amphiaraus
popCulture.description: The Argive seer swallowed by the earth before Thebes — oracle-hero of Oropos and father of Alcmaeon's revenge.

popCulture.title: Epigoni (play)
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: Sophocles' lost sequel where Amphiaraus' charge to Alcmaeon — avenge me on your mother — drives the next generation's war.
